raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  name: decord2
  version: "3.4.0"
  build_number: 2
  # Shell/variable references rendered per target platform, so a single script list works on both Unix (bash) and Windows (cmd.exe) without duplicated branches.
  prefix: ${{ "%LIBRARY_PREFIX%" if win else "$PREFIX" }}
  cmake_args: ${{ "%CMAKE_ARGS%" if win else "${CMAKE_ARGS}" }}
  cpu_count: ${{ "%CPU_COUNT%" if win else "${CPU_COUNT}" }}
  python: ${{ "%PYTHON%" if win else "$PYTHON" }}
  # CUDA is enabled for the cuda_compiler_version variants (12.x / 13.x) and off otherwise.
  use_cuda: ${{ "ON" if (cuda_compiler_version | default("None")) != "None" else "OFF" }}
  # The decord CMake target is created before enable_language(CUDA), so its CUDA_ARCHITECTURES property is never initialised from the CUDAARCHS activation variable.
  # Pass it explicitly to reuse the conda-forge default set.
  cuda_arch_flag: ${{ ("-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=" ~ ("%CUDAARCHS%" if win else "$CUDAARCHS")) if (cuda_compiler_version | default("None")) != "None" else "" }}
  # On Windows nvcuvid.lib is absent from the CUDA toolkit, so an import library is synthesized from the bundled .def and passed to CMake, which otherwise fails the NVDEC lookup.
  nvcuvid_lib_flag: ${{ "-DCUDA_NVCUVID_LIBRARY=%SRC_DIR%/nvcuvid.lib" if (win and use_cuda == "ON") else "" }}
  # Human-readable build string suffix that tells the CPU and CUDA builds of the compiled packages apart (e.g. "cpu" or "cuda129").
  cuda_build_string: ${{ "cpu" if (cuda_compiler_version | default("None")) == "None" else "cuda" + (cuda_compiler_version | replace(".", "")) }}
  # Solver penalty for the CPU variant (1) so the CUDA build (0) is preferred when both are installable.
  # Combined with the __cuda run constraint on libdecord2, this yields CUDA-preferred selection with a graceful fallback to CPU on machines without a GPU driver.
  cuda_variant_priority: ${{ 1 if (cuda_compiler_version | default("None")) == "None" else 0 }}
  # Inside an output build.string the build_number name resolves to a built-in that is not the effective build number,
  # so capture the context value here to embed it in the custom build strings below.
  build_number_string: ${{ build_number }}

recipe:
  name: decord2
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://github.com/johnnynunez/decord2/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: dc4b2510888a10f6fcc66e5ed7f36c8543c7f738b084a0116c4895f2945c122a
    patches:
      # Install the CMake export set into the prefix so downstream projects can use find_package(decord CONFIG).
      # Upstream only exports it into the build tree.
      - patches/0001-install-cmake-package-config.patch
      # Add the missing <cstdint> includes required by recent compilers that no longer pull it in transitively.
      - patches/0002-add-cstdint-includes.patch
      # Port the sources from the pre-0.4 dlpack API (DLContext / kDLGPU / DLTensor.ctx) to the modern one
      # (DLDevice / kDLCUDA / DLTensor.device) so decord2 builds against current dlpack.
      - patches/0003-modernize-dlpack-api.patch

build:
  number: ${{ build_number }}
  # Windows is skipped for now: the build is not yet validated there (the Windows-specific logic, e.g. the nvcuvid
  # import library, is kept in place for when it can be exercised on CI).
  # The VideoToolbox AV1 decode path uses kCMVideoCodecType_AV1, which requires the macOS 14 SDK, requested via conda_build_config.yaml.
  skip: win

outputs:
  # The library is compiled once in a staging output.
  # Each library package then selects its files, avoiding a rebuild per output.
  - staging:
      name: decord2-build
    build:
      script:
        # On Windows with CUDA, synthesize the nvcuvid import library from the bundled .def so the NVDEC symbols link.
        # The matching nvcuvid.dll ships with the driver and resolves at runtime.
        - if: win and use_cuda == "ON"
          then:
            - lib /def:scripts\nvcuvid.def /machine:x64 /out:%SRC_DIR%\nvcuvid.lib
        - cmake -G Ninja -S . -B build ${{ cmake_args }} -DUSE_CUDA=${{ use_cuda }} ${{ cuda_arch_flag }} ${{ nvcuvid_lib_flag }} -DFFMPEG_DIR=${{ prefix }}
        - cmake --build build --config Release --parallel ${{ cpu_count }}
        - cmake --install build --config Release
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - if: cuda_compiler_version != "None"
          then:
            - ${{ compiler('cuda') }}
        - cmake
        - ninja
      host:
        - ffmpeg
        # Decord2 uses the modern dlpack API (DLDevice / kDLCUDA / DLTensor.device), fully available since dlpack 0.5.
        - dlpack >=0.5
        # The public decord headers include <dmlc/...>, provided (header-only usage) by the conda-forge dmlc package.
        - dmlc
        # NVDEC (libnvcuvid) ships with the GPU driver rather than the CUDA toolkit, so it is absent at build time,
        # resolved at runtime, and therefore not a host dependency.
        - if: cuda_compiler_version != "None"
          then:
            - cuda-version ${{ cuda_compiler_version }}.*
            - cuda-cudart-dev
            - cuda-nvrtc-dev
            - libcublas-dev
            - cuda-nvml-dev
            - cuda-driver-dev

  - package:
      name: libdecord2
    inherit: decord2-build
    build:
      # Explicit build string suffix to tell the CPU and CUDA builds apart, plus the variant priority
      # that makes the solver prefer the CUDA build while __cuda (below) keeps it off driver-less machines.
      string: ${{ cuda_build_string }}_h${{ hash }}_${{ build_number_string }}
      variant:
        use_keys:
          - cuda_compiler_version
        down_prioritize_variant: ${{ cuda_variant_priority }}
      # The runtime package ships only the shared library.
      # The other platform's glob simply matches nothing.
      files:
        - lib/libdecord.*
        - Library/bin/decord.dll
    requirements:
      run:
        - if: cuda_compiler_version != "None"
          then:
            # The __cuda virtual package acts as a hardware lock: it keeps the prioritized CUDA build off
            # CPU-only machines, forcing a graceful fallback to the CPU build.
            - __cuda
    # ffmpeg and, when enabled, the CUDA runtime libraries are linked by libdecord and pinned into
    # this package by the run_exports inherited from the staging host dependencies.
    # No run_exports are declared here: downstream code builds against libdecord2-devel (headers),
    # so the version pin is exported from that package instead.
    tests:
      - package_contents:
          lib:
            - decord

  - package:
      name: libdecord2-devel
    inherit: decord2-build
    build:
      # Match the runtime build string so the CPU and CUDA development packages are distinguishable and
      # track their libdecord2 counterpart (pinned exact below).
      string: ${{ cuda_build_string }}_h${{ hash }}_${{ build_number_string }}
      variant:
        use_keys:
          - cuda_compiler_version
        down_prioritize_variant: ${{ cuda_variant_priority }}
      # The development package ships the headers and the CMake package config (plus the Windows import library).
      # Non-matching globs are ignored on the other platforms.
      files:
        - include/decord/**
        - lib/cmake/decord/**
        - Library/include/decord/**
        - Library/lib/cmake/decord/**
        - Library/lib/decord.lib
    requirements:
      run:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('libdecord2', exact=True) }}
        # The public headers include <dlpack/dlpack.h>, so consumers building against them need the dlpack headers.
        - dlpack >=0.5
        # The public headers also include <dmlc/...>, so consumers need the dmlc headers as well.
        - dmlc
      # libdecord.so ships no versioned SONAME and offers no ABI stability guarantees, so consumers building against the headers
      # must be pinned to the matching runtime build.
      run_exports:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('libdecord2', upper_bound='x.x.x') }}
    tests:
      - package_contents:
          include:
            - decord/video_interface.h
      # Check that a downstream project can find and link the library through find_package(decord CONFIG).
      - script:
          - cmake-package-check decord --targets decord::decord
        requirements:
          run:
            - cmake-package-check
            - ${{ compiler('c') }}
            - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}

  - package:
      name: decord2
    build:
      # Decord's Python bindings are pure Python and load libdecord through ctypes at runtime, so the package is architecture independent.
      # This output does not inherit the staging build: it compiles the bindings from source and depends on libdecord2 for the shared library.
      noarch: python
      script:
        env:
          # The setup.py script locates the shared library through this variable.
          # The library itself ships in libdecord2, installed in $PREFIX/lib on Unix and as the DLL in %LIBRARY_BIN% on Windows.
          DECORD_LIBRARY_PATH: ${{ "%LIBRARY_BIN%" if win else "$PREFIX/lib" }}
        content:
          # Upstream tags the wheel as platform specific via distclass=BinaryDistribution.
          # The conda package bundles no library (it is stripped below), so drop that to keep the wheel pure and the output noarch.
          - ${{ python }} -c "p = 'python/setup.py'; s = open(p).read(); open(p, 'w').write(s.replace('distclass=BinaryDistribution,', ''))"
          - ${{ python }} -m pip install ./python -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
          # Remove the shared library that setup.py bundles into the package, since it is provided by libdecord2 and located at runtime.
          - ${{ python }} -c "import os; d = os.path.join(os.environ['SP_DIR'], 'decord'); [os.remove(os.path.join(d, f)) for f in ('libdecord.so', 'libdecord.dylib', 'decord.dll') if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, f))]"
    requirements:
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - pip
        - setuptools
        - wheel
        - numpy
        # The libdecord2 runtime package must be present so setup.py can locate the shared library at build time.
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('libdecord2', upper_bound='x.x.x') }}
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - numpy
        # noarch packages do not inherit run_exports, so the libdecord2 runtime dependency (a version range, since the exact build is platform specific) is declared explicitly.
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('libdecord2', upper_bound='x.x.x') }}
    tests:
      # Importing decord loads libdecord through ctypes.
      # On CUDA variants the library links the NVIDIA driver stubs (libcuda, libnvidia-ml), which are only present on machines with a GPU driver,
      # so the import based tests run on the CPU variant that CI can execute.
      # The pip_check metadata check runs on every variant.
      - if: cuda_compiler_version | default("None") == "None"
        then:
          - python:
              imports:
                - decord
              pip_check: true
              python_version:
                - ${{ python_min }}.*
                - "*"
          - script:
              - python -c "from decord import VideoReader, AudioReader"
          # Upstream unit tests, with media fixtures copied from the source tree because they are not shipped in the package.
          # PyTorch is provided so the torch bridge is exercised. The other bridges (mxnet, tf, tvm) skip gracefully when their framework is absent.
          # Five audio tests are deselected because they assert exact sample counts that depend on the FFmpeg build rather than on decord.
          - script:
              - pytest -v tests/python/unittests/test_video_reader.py tests/python/unittests/test_av_reader.py tests/python/unittests/test_audio_reader.py tests/python/unittests/test_bridges.py
                --deselect tests/python/unittests/test_audio_reader.py::test_single_channel_audio_reader
                --deselect tests/python/unittests/test_audio_reader.py::test_double_channels_audio_reader
                --deselect tests/python/unittests/test_audio_reader.py::test_bytes_io
                --deselect tests/python/unittests/test_audio_reader.py::test_resample
                --deselect tests/python/unittests/test_audio_reader.py::test_channel_change
            requirements:
              run:
                # Pin to python_min so PyTorch (used by the torch bridge test) resolves reliably.
                - python ${{ python_min }}.*
                - pytest
                - pytorch
            files:
              source:
                - examples/flipping_a_pancake.mkv
                - tests/python/unittests/test_video_reader.py
                - tests/python/unittests/test_av_reader.py
                - tests/python/unittests/test_audio_reader.py
                - tests/python/unittests/test_bridges.py
                - tests/test_data/
                - tests/resources/audio/
        else:
          - python:
              pip_check: true

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/johnnynunez/decord2
  summary: Efficient, hardware accelerated video loader for deep learning
  description: |
    Decord2 is a high-performance, efficient video decoding and loading library
    for deep learning research, featuring smart shuffling, random frame access,
    GPU acceleration, and seamless integration with popular frameworks.
    This recipe builds the shared C++ library (libdecord2) and the Python bindings (decord2).
  license: Apache-2.0
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
  repository: https://github.com/johnnynunez/decord2
  documentation: https://github.com/johnnynunez/decord2

extra:
  feedstock-name: decord2
  recipe-maintainers:
    - diegoferigo
